chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A great matter occurs in my heart.' He said, 'Say, La ilaha illa Allah.' Jameel said, 'So whenever something occurred in my heart, I would say, La ilaha illa Allah, and it would go away from me.'

key_terms.أَمْرٌ عَظِيمٌ: A great matter (significant thought or doubt)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: How to remove distracting doubts or whispers from the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on *Waswas* (Satanic insinuations), this hadith highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) practical spiritual remedy for cognitive distractions. By affirming *La ilaha illa Allah*, the believer anchors the mind in divine unity, effectively neutralizing the psychological and spiritual noise of the self (*nafs*) and Satan. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *dhikr* as a primary tool for maintaining inner clarity and focus during worship.
